subject: RetentionPay: sudden latency & 5xx spike during peak — VPC handoff suspected
messages:
From: Lucas Pinto <lucas.p@retentionpay.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: ops@retentionpay.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden 3x latency + 5xx spike — are you seeing this?

Naomi,

We started seeing an abrupt 3x median latency and ~10% 5xx rate on our inference calls to Redwood around 10:55 PT. Errors are mostly 502/504 and the traces show long upstream TCP/TLS handshakes plus DNS timeouts before failing. We captured packet traces and a few example payloads — attached.

This is hitting checkout flows for a live A/B cohort and costs us conversions. Our on-call SRE notes there's a change in VPC peering routes around the same time (cloud provider ticket 987654). Can you confirm whether you have any planned network changes or if there's a known peering hiccup? We need an immediate mitigation and an exec-level contact — this is near-production revenue impact.

Lucas
CTO, RetentionPay

Attachments: retentionpay_traces_20290527.pcap (pcap), rp_error_samples_20290527.jsonl (jsonl)
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Lucas Pinto <lucas.p@retentionpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 3x latency + 5xx spike — are you seeing this?

Lucas — thank you for the traces and the heads-up. We are seeing elevated tail latency and 502/504s on the ingress side. No scheduled peering changes from our infra team in the window you shared. I'm looping in Soojin (SRE) and Marissa (CS) to triage and coordinate a customer-facing update.

Immediate plan:
- Soojin: can you snapshot our edge peering metrics, DNS resolver logs, and proxy connection pool around 10:45–11:10 PT?
- Marissa: I'll prepare a brief customer note and timing.

I'll follow up within 30 minutes with a status and any temporary mitigations (route pinning / fallback to alternate peering).

— Naomi
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 3x latency + 5xx spike — are you seeing this?

Naomi / Marissa — initial findings:
- Edge peering telemetry shows an increase in RTT and SYN retransmits for the ASN range used by RetentionPay between 10:52–11:05 PT.
- DNS: we observed ~2–3s resolution failures from one of our resolver clusters; fallback to secondary resolver worked but added latency.
- Proxy pool: connection churn increased; we hit a transient conntrack threshold on a subset of proxy hosts, which caused queued requests and a few 502s when upstream came back slower.

Likely root cause (working hypothesis): an upstream peering path change caused higher packet loss + DNS resolver timeouts; that, combined with our proxy conntrack pressure, produced the spike.

Short-term mitigations applied (11:33 PT):
- Forced diversion of RetentionPay traffic to an alternate peering fabric (route pinning).
- Increased DNS resolver pool and decreased TTL on internal cache for the account.
- Added ephemeral proxy instances to increase connection capacity for the affected route.

Impact: errors dropped to normal levels by 11:50 PT, median latency reduced from ~210ms to ~85ms. We kept the route pinning in place for monitoring.

Next actions: full packet-level correlation and confirm with cloud provider if their peering reroute caused the transient loss. I'll produce a technical incident summary by EOD.

— Soojin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lucas Pinto <lucas.p@retentionpay.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 3x latency + 5xx spike — are you seeing this?

Lucas — thanks for the quick signal and the packet capture. Naomi / Soojin applied mitigations and we see recovery in metrics. I know this event impacted checkout conversions — I'm proposing a brief incident postmortem and a follow-up meeting to review SLA credits if we confirm the outage window.

Could you share a short list of the most impacted time ranges and any customer-visible errors you captured? We'll include that in the incident write-up and loop in accounts for potential remediation (credits / engineering time).

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Sudden 3x latency + 5xx spike — are you seeing this?

Marissa / Team — thanks for the fast response and route pinning. Impact window (based on our telemetry): 10:54–11:34 PT. Attached are error samples and a short list of checkout session ids that failed. We'll be available for a postmortem tomorrow morning.

Lucas
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Lucas Pinto <lucas.p@retentionpay.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident exec summary: RetentionPay peak path instability and remediation

Lucas — follow-up and exec summary after the EOD analysis and cross-cloud confirmation.

Summary (what happened):
- Symptom: median latency spike (x3) and sustained 5xx (~10%) impacting inference requests for RetentionPay between 10:54–11:34 PT on 2029-05-27.
- Root cause: a transient peering reroute by the cloud provider increased packet loss for the customer’s origin ASN. That led to DNS resolver timeouts on one of our resolver clusters, amplifying perceived upstream slowness. Concurrently, a subset of proxy hosts hit conntrack/connection churn which increased queuing and produced 502/504 responses.

What we did (timing):
- 11:33 PT: route pinning to alternate peering fabric; increased DNS resolver capacity; ephemeral proxy capacity added.
- 11:50 PT: metrics returned to baseline.

Customer impact: checkout flows for an A/B cohort experienced failures; RetentionPay measured conversion loss during the 40-minute window.

Preventative & follow-up items:
1) Peering resilience: expand multihoming for critical customer ASNs and monitor ASN-level loss with automatic reroute triggers. (Owner: Networking — target Q3 2029)
2) DNS hardening: add cross-cluster resolver failover + health checks to avoid single-resolver TTL amplification. (Owner: Infra — target 6 weeks)
3) Proxy scaling: implement connection backpressure controls and early shedding to avoid conntrack saturation. (Owner: SRE — target 30 days)
4) SLA/credits: Marissa to coordinate with Customer Success and Sales (Vivek/Aditya) on potential credit and commercial remediation.

We're happy to present a technical deep-dive to your engineering team and coordinate timeline for changes that reduce recurrence risk.

— Naomi Feldman
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_timeline_20290527.pdf (summary), retentionpay_traces_20290527.pcap (pcap)
